note: Standard DSAR scopings. Every template narrows an existing query and none replaces it. The vocabulary in the employment-file sweep is a matter of local practice — correct it here rather than in code. `verified` records the date each template's KQL was called against a real tenant; see verification/kql-property-probe-2026-08-02.md for the measurements, including the finding that mail-item properties silently exclude site content.

templates.name: Time-boxed scope
templates.purpose: Limit the search to the period the request covers.
templates.guidance: Mail items carry `sent`; SharePoint and OneDrive items carry `lastmodifiedtime`. This scopes on both, because scoping on `sent` alone silently drops every file in range — a miss a DSAR response cannot afford.

inputs.name: start
inputs.label: From
inputs.help: Leave blank for no lower bound.

inputs.name: end
inputs.label: To
inputs.help: Leave blank for no upper bound.

templates.name: Workload split
templates.purpose: Count one workload at a time, to see where the effort and the cost actually are.
templates.guidance: Run this once per workload and compare the counts before committing to an export. Because this tool reports counts rather than content, a per-workload breakdown is the cheapest planning information available — and export bills by volume on E3. Measured on a real estate, meetings were 28 of 40 hits: a naive count is often dominated by calendar items.
templates.caution: `kind:` is a mail-item property. Measured 2026-08-02: adding any `kind:` clause reduced the site count to zero, including on a query that touches three sites — so this counts mailbox content only and silently excludes SharePoint and OneDrive. Use it to split the mail workload, never to conclude how much there is in total.

templates.name: Employment file
templates.purpose: The vocabulary an employment-dispute DSAR usually turns on.
templates.guidance: By far the most common context for a DSAR is an employment dispute. These are free-text clauses, so they catch a document discussing the subject even where the subject was never a participant — which is the class of item a participants-only search cannot reach.
templates.caution: This narrows to items using this vocabulary. It is a triage aid, not the whole response: a DSAR covers all personal data, not only the contested part.

inputs.name: terms
inputs.label: Additional terms
inputs.help: Comma or newline separated. Local vocabulary matters — a policy name or an internal scheme title often finds more than the generic terms do.

templates.name: Privilege triage
templates.purpose: Surface candidates for the legal-privilege exemption.
templates.guidance: Add your legal team's address or domain to catch correspondence that never uses the words. Addresses become `participants:` clauses automatically.
templates.caution: This finds candidates. It does not decide privilege, and nothing here should be withheld on the strength of a keyword match — the exemption is a legal judgement with a documented rationale.

templates.name: Third-party co-occurrence
templates.purpose: Items involving both the subject and someone else — the redaction workload.
templates.guidance: In a grievance or a dispute this is the awkward set: material that is the subject's personal data and somebody else's at the same time. Sizing it early tells you how much redaction the response actually needs.
templates.caution: Third-party data is not automatically exempt. The test is whether disclosure is reasonable in the circumstances, which is a decision per item and not a property of this search.

inputs.name: people
inputs.label: Other party
inputs.help: Names and addresses, comma separated. An address becomes a `participants:` clause; a name becomes a free-text mention.

templates.name: Attachments and file types
templates.purpose: Size the attachment volume before committing to an export.
templates.guidance: Export is the one operation that bills on E3, and it bills by volume. Attachments are usually where that volume is.
templates.caution: Like `kind:`, this behaved as a mail-item property when measured on 2026-08-02 — the site count went to zero. Treat the result as an attachment count within mailboxes, not a file count across the estate.

inputs.name: filetypes
inputs.label: File types
inputs.help: Letters and digits only. A file type is not quoted in KQL, so it is the one value that cannot be made safe by quoting — anything else is refused.
